overview_raw: Are you looking to upskill quickly for a career switch, re-enter the workforce, or work in web development? The BCIT Front-End Web Developer certificate program offers job-ready skills in just six months. It is ideal for those with little to no knowledge of web development and you have the option to do the program online or in person. Delivery: blended. See details . About the program A dynamic, full-time, 6-month program where you’ll learn by doing — no exams, just real projects that mirror the work of professional web developers. Work in teams on hands-on, project-based assignments that simulate real-world development environments. Offered online, in-person at Downtown, Vancouver or blended for those who prefer a mix. Collaborate, share knowledge, and build a lasting professional network with your cohort and alumni. Commit to a Monday–Friday schedule (9:30 am to 4:00 pm), and graduate with a recognized certificate. Benefit from a strong job placement rate once you graduate. See the Program Details to learn more about what to expect from FWD, and how to prepare for a career in web development. This program is for you if… You’ve done other things , and now you’re ready to bring that experience into the world of web development. You’re a career changer looking to build on your past education, work, or life experience by gaining in-demand web development skills. You want to learn web development in a structured, supportive, and hands-on environment that sets you up for success. You’re ready to transition into a web development career in just six months, with a program designed to get you job-ready fast. You want to combine your existing skills — whether in customer service, project management, design, journalism, marketing, or other fields — with new technical expertise to create a powerful, versatile career path. You already hold a credential in another field (related or not) and are ready to pivot into a future-focused career in web development. If any of these sound like you, please check the Entrance Requirements to ensure you can apply and start your new web developer career path! After graduating… When you graduate, you’ll be ready to launch your career in web development with a professional portfolio that showcases the real-world projects you’ve built throughout the program. Your new skills and experience can lead to roles such as: Front-End Developer JavaScript Developer UX/UI Designer or Specialist WordPress Developer or Consultant Freelance Web Developer You’ll also be equipped to take on freelance clients or even start your own web development business, building websites for small businesses or collaborating with agencies. Visit the Graduating and Jobs page to discover five compelling reasons to become a Front-End Web Developer. Next up Entrance Requirements

program_details_raw: Skills you’ll learn The front-end web developer program prides itself on teaching the skills necessary to start a career as a front-end web developer. Our curriculum evolves with industry demands, ensuring you’re always learning the skills that employers value most. HTML & CSS At the core of every web page are two key technologies: HTML, which structures the content, and CSS, which styles its appearance. You’ll learn the fundamentals of semantic HTML to follow best practices for accessibility and search engine optimization (SEO). Using the knowledge and best practices learned from their design and UX courses, you’ll learn how to style websites using CSS to build user-friendly websites. JavaScript & React The first programming language you’ll learn is the one that adds interactivity to websites and web apps: JavaScript. After learning the fundamentals of JavaScript, you’ll learn more advanced JavaScript with React, the most popular JavaScript framework, to build advanced web applications utilizing APIs to populate dynamic content. User Experience / User Interface Design (UX/UI) Some websites just work — they’re intuitive, easy to navigate, and visually appealing. That’s the power of a great user experience . It is why UX/UI is a critical component in creating successful websites and applications. You’ll learn the foundations of UX — how to define user requirements, design effective information architecture, and evaluate solutions through usability testing. The program emphasizes both the theory and practical application of UX. To bring interfaces to life, you’ll also explore graphic design principles and gain hands-on experience with industry-standard tools like Photoshop, Illustrator, Adobe XD, and Figma. PHP & MySQL To build dynamic, data-driven websites, front-end developers need to understand how the front end communicates with servers and databases. That’s where PHP and MySQL come in. PHP is a server-side language used on over 70% of all websites. MySQL is the most common database management system on the web. These skills, which are covered in the program, can lead to becoming a full-stack web developer should you choose that path. Utilize AI effectively As AI tools become increasingly integrated into the web development workflow, they’re proving to be valuable assets for boosting development efficiency and accelerating learning. In the Front-End Web Developer program, you’re guided in using AI tools effectively for web development — learning how to leverage them for learning, while understanding their boundaries, limitations, and ethical concerns. Through hands-on practice, learners will use AI models and agents, such as ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, and Claude, to enhance their development skills and productivity. For example: Efficiency : Leverage AI-powered code completion to handle repetitive tasks, freeing up time for higher-level problem-solving. Debugging : Use AI to identify errors, suggest fixes, and streamline troubleshooting. Learning : Treat AI as a coding tutor — get explanations, explore unfamiliar concepts, and access relevant documentation. Despite what you may have heard, AI models are not a replacement for a developer. Instead, they are tools to improve development efficiency. They require human input at the start and human verification at the end. AI models are productivity tools that lack creativity, empathy, judgment and the ability to know if what they suggest even works! Skilled developers remain essential for designing and evaluating development solutions that meet user needs. The human touch remains at the core of front-end web development. See also the interview we had with faculty Jonathon Leathers about how artificial intelligence is reshaping the profession – and what that means for students, employers, and the future of the web . Tooling Web development isn’t just about writing code — it’s also about using the right tools to work efficiently and professionally. You’ll gain experience with the essential tools that modern developers rely on to build, test, and manage websites and web applications, and will learn how to: Use version control systems like Git and GitHub to track changes, collaborate with teammates, and manage your codebase. Set up and customize your code editor (like Visual Studio Code) to streamline your workflow and boost productivity. Navigate the command line to interact with your development environment and run essential tools. Integrate JavaScript build tools (like Vite) to automate tasks and speed up development. Understand how these tools fit into a professional workflow, from solo projects to team-based development. By the end of the program, you’ll be comfortable using the tools and workflows that are standard in the web development industry. Content Management Systems & E-Commerce You’ll learn how to create custom WordPress themes and plugins to practice building websites for businesses while learning the fundamentals of a CMS. Over 40% of all websites on the internet use WordPress as their content management system (CMS), and the Front-end Web Developer program teaches custom WordPress development to meet this demand. After learning how to build websites with a CMS, you’ll take it a step further to learn how to build online stores using the two most popular platforms: Shopify and WooCommerce. Managing web projects While web developers typically don’t begin their careers as project managers, they are often part of collaborative teams working on a variety of projects. In this program, you’ll gain an understanding of common project management processes and methodologies — including waterfall and agile — that are widely used in the web development field. This foundational knowledge helps you contribute effectively to team-based projects and understand how development work fits into the broader project lifecycle. Portfolio and career management Towards the end of the program, you’ll focus on planning a career in front-end web development. You’re helped to build a compelling resume and LinkedIn profile and prepare to showcase a body of digital work created both in and outside the classroom. Through guided research, you’ll explore industry trends, employment opportunities, and entrepreneurial paths to develop a personalized career plan. As part of this process, they also create a fully functional, professional-level portfolio website — a public showcase of their skills, aligned with their career goals and industry expectations. Capstone project The final course in the program is a team-based project where you’ll apply the full range of skills you’ve developed — from user experience and interface design to development and project management. Working in teams, you’ll build a website for a specific business of their choosing. This Capstone Project replicates a real-world web development scenario, focusing on meeting client needs through a custom website or online store. Project and team-based learning The Front-End Web Developer program uses a hands-on and project-based approach to learning. There are no exams. Instead, you’ll complete assignments, solo projects, and team projects that mimic web development projects they will encounter in their careers. Because employers are looking for individuals with technical and communication skills, you’ll learn how to work effectively in a team by utilizing best practices for project management and communication. Community: Finding and participating in the right circles Building a strong professional network is just as important as building technical skills. In FWD, you’ll have opportunities to connect with classmates, alumni, and industry professionals, forming relationships that can lead to mentorship, collaboration, and career opportunities. You’ll also learn where to find and how to engage with online and local tech communities, meetups, and professional groups. Collaborative growth : After completing the program, many graduates continue working together on portfolio projects — and in some cases, launch businesses. Industry exposure : You’ll attend events where they connect with employers, developers, UX designers, marketers, and business owners. These events can lead to job offers, freelance work, and valuable mentorship. Alumni connections : Graduates return to share their experiences , offering current students insights into job hunting, breaking into the industry, and building a career. Network effect : You’re encouraged to build strong relationships with peers and alumni — many companies that hire one graduate return to hire more, based on the quality of their work and trusted referrals. Program length 28 weeks, full-time. Grading Students must obtain a minimum of 65% in each course in order to proceed to the next course. All courses must be passed in order to qualify for the final capstone project. Program delivery Blended: This program is delivered partly on campus and partly online. Students will have the choice of either physically attending class or participating online. For instance, if class starts at 9:30 am, the instructor will be in class teaching and will also be available live online to those who opt to participate remotely. This program is run as a cohort model with instruction in the morning and mandatory labs in the afternoon. Program location Downtown Campus 555 Seymour Street Vancouver, BC Distance and online learning Go back Courses Next up Graduating & Jobs

courses.course_overview_raw: Students will learn the basics of front-end web development, code management, and the tools of web development including version control using Git and GitHub . Course topics and activities include a review of the web in general, how it works from the internet layer to the application layer, and how to create basic multi-page web sites. Students will register a domain name, secure their own web space and learn to operate basic web services including File transfer (FTP) and admin features. S udents will also review the latest versions of HTML and CSS. Learning will focus on web standards as outlined by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) to cod e HTM L and CSS to control hierarchy structure, functionality, layout and appearance of websites while creating modern, standards compliant, semantic and accessible markup for a web site. The coding process from design to publishing a web site to the public internet will be covered. Evaluation will include lab assignments and projects. ​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course covers the theory and best practices of web design fundamentals. Topics include screen-design principles; web layout and design; digital colour theory; typography fundamentals; image and web graphics sourcing, handling and copyright. Students will learn the best practices in creating designs for responsive web sites that adapt to different screen sizes using the fundamental design and usability principles for layout, such as visual hierarchy, colours, fonts, readability, proportions, alignments, and white space. In this class, students will explore in detail the differences between raster and vector graphics and basic techniques suitable for digital image creation, manipulation, and management. Students will develop practical skills will be developed in how to colour correct, resize, and resample images as well as how to use transparency settings and automate the resizing and saving of large numbers of images for the web. Evaluation will include lab assignments. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: User Experience (UX) plays a critical role in the success of products and services. This course will focus on the theory of website UX planning, the design process, and the integration of UX into the web design and development process. Students will learn the fundamentals of defining requirements, creating information architecture, and evaluating solutions using usability testing techniques. This course will use a combination of lectures, in-class discussions, hands-on exercises, group work, and tool demonstrations. Evaluation will include a combination of group and individual assignments. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Modern web sites and applications demand dynamically and constantly updated content and interactive user interfaces. This course introduces the JavaScript programming language as well as foundational programming concepts to provide the services and features that industry demands. Students will be introduced to general computer programming concepts such as variables, conditional statements, loops, functions, objects and classes. By applying these basic programming concepts students will explore the development of interactive web experiences such as slide shows, animated navigation systems, tabs, accordions, lightboxes and other common web widgets. Manipulating and traversing an HTML document with JavaScript using the browser's DOM API will also be discussed.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course covers how to use Generative AI (GenAI) tools to enhance learning and increase productivity while working on web development and design projects. The three-day course will be spread across multiple months to integrate with more advanced topics learned later in the FWD program. The first class will focus on what GenAI is and how to use GenAI tools for learning. In the second class, students will learn how to use GenAI tools for code review and how to use agentic GenAI for code creation. In the final class, students will form small teams and attempt to build a new, complex web project entirely with GenAI to assess the feasibility of the process and the quality of the result. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: (65% in FWDP 1000 and 65% in FWDP 1100 and 65% in FWDP 1200)
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course focuses on collaborative front-end web development practices used in modern team environments. Building on prior studies, students will learn how to integrate user-centered thinking, design systems, and front-end web development techniques into a collaborative workflow using industry-standard tools. Students will practice how to collaboratively manage code using version control systems such as GitHub, including branching, merging, pull requests, and code reviews. Students will work with collaborative UX design tools to create, interpret, and implement information architecture, design systems, components, and high-fidelity mock-ups, translating design specifications into functional and accessible user interfaces. Students will be introduced to project management tools to support task organization, team coordination, and workflow planning in a collaborative setting, working through an end-to-end design-to-development process. Prerequisite(s): (65% in FWDP 1000 and 65% in FWDP 1100 and 65% in FWDP 1200)

This course is an overview of common project management concepts which will be applied to the collaborative projects in the later courses. The course includes the basic concepts of web project management, teamwork, and an introduction to popular project management software applications used in the web development field. Students will apply their knowledge and skills as well as appropriate tools and techniques to project activities to meet project requirements in later courses. Students will engage in project planning, identify project stakeholders, define the roles and responsibilities of the team, define project scope, devise risk and quality plans, map out schedules, and learn about time tracking and documentation. Evaluation will include in-class assignments. Prerequisite(s): FWDP 1000

This course shifts the focus from client-side to server-side programming utilizing PHP and MySQL. An introduction to PHP fundamentals and the role it plays in generating dynamic websites will be covered. Students will explore the differences between client-side and server-side scripting, learning to identify when scripting solutions are appropriate. They will apply basic scripting techniques, write and use functions, validate HTML forms, utilize regular expressions, and implement cookie management and session handling. Additionally, students will learn to design and implement relational databases using MySQL, write basic SQL queries for data manipulation, and use PHP to interact with and manage databases. Evaluation will include assignments and a project. Prerequisite(s): FWDP 1000

The Web Scripting 3 course introduces students to JavaScript-based web application development. The course explores setting up and developing a web application using modern JavaScript build systems. Students will learn how to implement modern coding methodologies available in JavaScript such as modules and classes. Application state management will be explored in detail along with routing, validating user data and styling modules. Utilizing foundational JavaScript skills and modern JavaScript coding and build system techniques, students will explore developing and deploying full-featured web applications. Prerequisite(s): FWDP 1000 and FWDP 1400

This course covers the fundamental features of dynamic websites and the creation of custom-coded websites built with a Content Management System (CMS). Students will learn the basics of dynamic websites, how they are used to create a CMS, and how to work with a CMS to build websites. Students will create, configure, and migrate websites built using a CMS. Once they understand the basic features, students will create custom code to extend functionality, edit and create templates, and build a basic web app or website on a CMS. To prepare them for their Capstone Project, students will also create a development plan for a mock client website. Evaluation will include lab assignments and projects. Prerequisite(s): 65% in FWDP 1000 and 65% in FWDP 2400

This course focuses on the multiple platforms and solutions that can be used to create and launch an online store. These include open source and Software as a Service (SaaS) platforms to provide a foundation for work with e-commerce solutions Course topics include all stages of the preparation, configuration, and setup of a secure online store. Students will determine the appropriate tools necessary to configure and securely operate an online store for various products and services. Learners will then review tool features, configure settings for product samples, price options, and manage shipping options. Students will also learn and use the relevant templating or theming languages and methods to customize the design, layout, and functionality of their online store and further customize functionality using extensions. Once the store is set up, students will use best practices to secure the store, connect payment gateways, and test the payment process to complete the entire e-commerce purchasing process. Evaluation will include assignments. Prerequisite(s): FWDP 3600

courses.prerequisite_raw: 65% in FWDP 1000 and 65% in FWDP 1100 and 65% in FWDP 1200
courses.course_overview_raw: The focus of this course is to plan a front-end web development-related career, and at the same time, prepare to showcase a body of digital work created in and outside the program. This includes personal and professional development designed to support career success. Students will research trends, employment, and entrepreneurship to create a career plan. They will also create a fully functional, publicly accessible, professional-level portfolio website based on after-program career goals and industry expectations. At the end of the course project, students will have a portfolio website that demonstrates their skills using HTML5, CSS, JavaScript, JavaScript frameworks, and optionally server-side programming and/or content management systems. Students will also develop their personal brand, create a competitive resume and cover letter and learn advanced interview skills. Evaluation will include the project and workshop participation. Prerequisite(s): 65% in FWDP 1000 and 65% in FWDP 1100 and 65% in FWDP 1200

courses.prerequisite_raw: 65% in FWDP 2100 and 65% in FWDP 2300 and 65% in FWDP 3700
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course is the culmination of the knowledge and learning in the Front-End Web Development program and the practical application and development of skills gained in earlier courses. This course will introduce students to the professional practice of working on a small web development team to build a mid-sized custom dynamic website. Throughout the supervised project, students will use industry best practices to develop a website based on specific business and functional requirements. To manage their tasks and meet deadlines, students will work collaboratively using communication and management tools common in the industry. All teams will have scheduled meetings with the instructor to track their progress and will present tutorials to the class on topics they research during their projects. Evaluation will be based on the project. Evaluation will be based on the project. Prerequisite(s): 65% in FWDP 2100 and 65% in FWDP 2300 and 65% in FWDP 3700
